title: Reciting in prayer
hookLine: a short surah after the Fatiha in the first two units

lines: SUNSET, AT THE BACK OF A MOSQUE.
cards: The back of a mosque at sunset. The imam's voice rises: first the Fatiha, the seven verses said in every prayer. Then a pause, and something else.
Tonight it's a surah about daybreak. Tomorrow it might be the one about the elephant, or the orphan, or the soul.
Around the room, some who couldn't order lunch in Arabic follow every word, because they learned these short surahs as children. That's where Juz' 'Amma lives.
Not on a shelf, but in the mouths of people praying, all over the world.

teach.b: Each prayer is made of units, rak'ahs: standing, bowing, prostrating, sitting. In every unit, standing, the one praying recites the Fatiha.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said, in a hadith Bukhari records, that there is no prayer for the one who doesn't recite the opening of the Book.

teach.h: A SHORT SURAH IN THE FIRST TWO.
teach.b: In the first two units, something is added: a short surah, or a few verses from anywhere in the Qur'an. In the third and fourth, the Fatiha alone.
The schools of law weigh the addition differently: the Hanafi school counts it as required, and the others count it as a strongly recommended practice of the Prophet.

At dawn, sunset and night, the imam recites aloud in the first two units; at noon and afternoon, silently. So people need a store of short surahs, and Juz' 'Amma is the store. Two stories show the spirit of it.

teach.h: MU'ADH IS TOLD: KEEP IT SHORTER.
teach.b: A companion named Mu'adh led his people in prayer with such a long surah that a tired man left. The Prophet corrected him and named shorter ones instead, like By the sun and By the night.
Another man, leading prayer, added Say, He is Allah, the One, every single time. People mentioned it to the Prophet.
Asked why, the man said it describes the Most Merciful, and he loved to recite it.
The Prophet said: tell him that Allah loves him. In that report, a short surah said with love is answered with love.

how: In each unit of the prayer Muslims recite al-Fatiha, and in the first two units they add a short surah or some verses, often from Juz' 'Amma; the imam recites aloud at dawn, sunset and night, and silently at noon and afternoon.

o: one unit of the prayer, named for bowing

games.q: a man leading prayer adds Say, He is Allah, the One, every time. people complain. what does the Prophet say?
o: tell him to vary his surahs
tell him that Allah loves him
tell him to stop leading prayer
games.why: the man said he loved it because it describes the Most Merciful. the Prophet said: tell him that Allah loves him (Bukhari).

practice: Choose one short surah you don't yet know by heart; Al-Kawthar has only three verses, and so does Al-'Asr. Read it slowly in whatever language you have, then again, letting one line settle on each breath.
If you pray, you can say it after the Fatiha in one of tonight's prayers, even slowly, with a glance at the page; if you don't, you can simply listen to it recited once today.

wordCard.voice: Rak'ah, one unit of the prayer: the Fatiha is recited in every one, and a short surah follows in the first two, which is why Juz' 'Amma is heard so often.

orig.note: Arabic: one unit of the prayer, named for the bowing (ruku').

carryVoice: Your line: a new one tonight. The Fatiha stays; the surah after it is yours to choose. See you tomorrow.
